title: Tata Motors EV Bookings Triple as Company Bets on Record Festive Quarter
excerpt: India's largest EV maker has seen a three-fold surge in electric vehicle bookings over six months but faces supply constraints as it targets the industry's biggest-ever September-December quarter.
body:
• Tata Motors EV bookings have tripled over the last six months, with one in three new bookings now for electric vehicles
  • Production is constrained by battery cell supply bottlenecks, with the company ramping capacity from 10,000 to 15,000 units per month
  • Q1 FY27 saw 46% overall passenger vehicle growth and 77% EV growth year-on-year, with EV penetration hitting a record 23%
  • A price hike of up to ₹25,000 takes effect September 1 as input cost inflation squeezed Q1 net profit by 80%

Tata Motors is riding an unprecedented surge in electric vehicle demand but finds itself in an unusual position: the constraint is not consumer appetite but the company's own ability to produce fast enough. EV bookings have tripled over the past six months, and the company is now betting that the upcoming festive season will deliver the Indian auto industry's largest-ever quarter.

Vivek Srivatsa, Chief Commercial Officer of Tata Passenger Electric Mobility Ltd, confirmed the scale of the demand spike in an interview with PTI. "We had 3x growth in bookings for EVs, and we are only restricted by our production capability," he said, adding that Tata has been gaining EV market share every month over the past two to three months.

Production Bottlenecks Hold Back Growth

While internal factory capacity is not the primary issue, the company is struggling with supply-side hurdles — particularly in securing imported battery cells. The most significant bottlenecks are linked to imports from China, which have hindered Tata's ability to deliver vehicles at the pace of demand.

The company is working to ramp up monthly EV production from 10,000 units to 15,000 over the next few months. Officials expect the battery supply constraints to ease by the end of the September 2026 quarter, which would position Tata to better capitalize on the festive demand surge.

In May 2026, Tata crossed the 10,000-unit monthly EV sales mark for the first time, recording 10,517 units — an 85% year-on-year increase. The company holds roughly 39% of India's passenger EV market, widening its lead over Mahindra (23%) and JSW MG Motor (19%).

Record Growth, Shrinking Margins

The demand boom has come alongside financial pressure. In Q1 FY27, Tata Motors' net profit fell 80% to ₹775 crore, driven primarily by high input cost inflation that has squeezed margins across the auto sector.

To stabilize profitability, the company has announced price increases of up to ₹25,000 across its vehicle portfolio, including its electric range, effective September 1, 2026. Srivatsa said he does not expect the hike to materially affect festive-season sales, though the longer-term impact remains uncertain.

"Price hikes have been fairly recent. I would say that the price hike should not affect the festive season, but longer term, what happens after festive season is something we'll have to watch out for."

— Vivek Srivatsa, CCO, Tata Passenger Electric Mobility

Festive Season Could Be Industry's Biggest Ever

The Q1 FY27 numbers set the stage for what Tata expects to be a blockbuster September-December period. The broader passenger vehicle industry grew 46% year-on-year in Q1, while EVs grew even faster at 77%. One in three new Tata bookings is now for an electric vehicle, up sharply from a year ago.

Srivatsa attributed the sustained demand momentum to multiple factors: the GST 2.0 reforms implemented in September 2025, which maintained the 5% tax rate on EVs while reducing the rate on small cars from 28% to 18%; rising fuel prices driven by geopolitical tensions in West Asia; and a growing consumer shift toward on-road family travel.

"If I look at the months of July and August, the momentum seems to continue, and that means the festive season, indications are that it's going to be extremely positive, quite likely to be the largest quarter for the industry," Srivatsa said.

Investor Watch Points

Tata's EV portfolio spans the Nexon EV, Punch EV, Tiago EV, Curvv EV, and the recently launched Sierra EV with quad-wheel drive. The breadth of the lineup — covering sub-₹5 lakh to ₹19 lakh segments — has been key to capturing demand across price points.

For investors and market watchers, the coming quarter will test whether Tata can resolve supply bottlenecks in time to convert its booking backlog into deliveries, and whether the price hike stalls momentum once the festive premium fades. Srivatsa acknowledged that year-on-year percentage growth may taper as the base effect from last year's post-GST surge kicks in, but stressed that absolute sales numbers should remain "extremely high."
